name: Wisp wide-area IR sensor (Anduril)
description: Passive 360 deg wide-area infrared sensor with on-edge AI. Searches for low, slow, small UAS without a radar cue and feeds Lattice. Detection band 3-10 miles; 4.8 km is the low end.

classifyRangeM.condition: classification range — No separate classification range is published. WISP is documented to 'detect, classify and continuously track drones while reducing false alarms generated by birds or environmental clutter' - the detection event IS the classifier output, so classification is modeled as available wherever detection is. Set equal to detectRangeM.
classifyRangeM.source: U.S. Deploys Anduril Counter-Drone System to Strengthen Homeland Defense Against Drone Threats

sectorDeg.source: Anduril Wisp product page (embedded page JSON, curl)

elevationDeg.condition: field of view, elevation — The 125 deg vertical extent is published but the datum (how it is split above and below the horizon) is not. Writing [min,max] would require inventing the split, so the field stays null and the extent is recorded here.
elevationDeg.source: Anduril to use artificial intelligence (AI) and sensor fusion for IR-based counter-UAV perimeter security
elevationDeg.note: Inventory records null deg (125 deg (vertical FOV extent)) at UNKNOWN L3; the seed leaves the field null

maxAltitudeFt.condition: detection range, large manned aircraft — This is a DIFFERENT target class (airliner-sized, high thermal contrast) and must never be read as a small-UAS range. It shows coverage extends at least to 12,000 ft but no ceiling is published, so the field stays null. Recorded only; RangeBoard reads no altitude.
maxAltitudeFt.source: Anduril to use artificial intelligence (AI) and sensor fusion for IR-based counter-UAV perimeter security
maxAltitudeFt.note: Inventory records null ft (commercial aircraft at 12,000 ft from about 93 miles ft / miles) at REPORTED L3; the seed leaves the field null

eoBand.value: thermal: passive infrared detection and tracking
